tier_reason: The numbers come from the uWS author's own Feb 2021 blog post (106k vs 8.8k req/s against Node.js/Fastify cluster). The uWS side uses public code (examples/HelloWorldThreaded.cpp driven by uSockets examples/http_load_test.c) on a Raspberry Pi 4. Compiler and flags are not stated, and the Node.js/Fastify side (versions, server code) is not published, so this is first-party with partial methodology: C, not A or B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 12x HTTP req/s vs Node.js/Fastify cluster: 106k vs 8.8k req/s (non-pipelined, 200 connections, Raspberry Pi 4 overclocked to arm_freq=1750); uWS with TLS 1.3 at 77k req/s = 8.75x vs cleartext Fastify
corrections.workload: Non-pipelined 'Hello world' HTTP GET, 200 connections, generated by uSockets http_load_test on a laptop over Ethernet; server is uWS HelloWorldThreaded on a fanless Raspberry Pi 4, compared with Node.js/Fastify run as a cluster on the same Pi
corrections.hardware: Raspberry Pi 4 (4 cores, passively cooled, overclocked from 1.5 GHz with over_voltage=2, arm_freq=1750), Ubuntu Server 20.10 ARM64; load generator on a separate laptop over Ethernet
corrections.caveats: The 12x figure is 106k vs 8.8k req/s from a single first-party run in the uWS author's own blog post (Alex Hultman, Level Up Coding, 2021-02-03), on an overclocked Raspberry Pi 4. Node.js and Fastify versions and the Fastify server code are not published, and compiler/flags are not stated. The workload is a hello-world HTTP server comparison, not an event-loop microbenchmark. The original levelup.gitconnected.com URL returns HTTP 403 to bots; the Wayback snapshot 20220510081241 is readable. The repo's older benchmarks/README.md chart (uWS v0.15 vs Node.js 10.13, CPU-time normalized) shows a smaller gap: about 6x (derived from page data, bar heights read approximately as ~180k vs ~28k req/s). Licensing: the README says 'Intellectual property, all rights reserved' and that Apache-2.0 applies only where an explicit notice is given. src/ClientApp.h, src/Http3*.h and src/LocalCluster.h carry no license header, and src/MoveOnlyFunction.h is third-party MIT.

notes: The 12x claim was verified at its source through the Wayback Machine (direct levelup and medium.com URLs return 403). The ratio holds: 106k/8.8k = 12.0x. Its baseline is specifically Node.js with Fastify in cluster mode, so baseline, workload, hardware and benchmark_url were corrected; the tier stays C. Metadata checked: Apache-2.0, not archived, not a fork, 18,992 stars, last commit 2026-09-18, and 'mixed' usability is confirmed by the unlicensed src headers.
